Compute effective neighbourhood size for each row of a weight matrix

effective_neighbourhood_size.Rd

For each row \(w_i\), the effective neighbourhood size is defined as \(n_{\mathrm{eff},i} = \exp(H(w_i))\), where \(H(w_i) = -\sum_j w_{ij} \log w_{ij}\) is the Shannon entropy. This equals the number of equally-weighted neighbours that would produce the same entropy.

Usage

effective_neighbourhood_size(W, eps = 1e-12)

Arguments

W

A square row-stochastic weight matrix (or will be row-normalised).

eps

Small positive value to avoid log(0).

Value

A numeric vector of length nrow(W) containing \(n_{\mathrm{eff},i}\).
